cards.q: What is POP3 and how does it handle mail?
cards.a: POP3 (TCP 110) downloads email from a server to a single client and typically removes it from the server, making it a simple offline download-and-go protocol; its secure variant is POP3S on TCP 995.
The client pulls mail from the server (port 110, secure 995), mail is stored client-locally with the server usually emptied, it is offline, and there is no synchronization across clients.

cards.q: How do POP3 and IMAP compare?
cards.a: POP3 downloads mail and typically deletes it from the server, has poor multi-device support, is offline, uses a single INBOX, and uses ports 110/995; IMAP keeps mail on the server, syncs across devices, is online, uses server folders, and uses ports 143/993.

cards.q: What does a basic POP3 session look like?
cards.a: USER/PASS authenticate, LIST lists messages with numbers, RETR n downloads a message, DELE n marks one for deletion, and QUIT finalizes the session, with deletions applied at QUIT.

cards.q: When does POP3 actually delete a marked message?
cards.a: Deletions marked with DELE are finalized when the client sends QUIT at session close.

cards.q: What are the POP3 ports and security modes?
cards.a: 110 is plaintext and 995 is POP3S over TLS; mail credentials should not cross on 110, so 995 (or STARTTLS) is required.

cards.q: When should you choose POP3 versus IMAP?
cards.a: Choose POP3 for a single client, low server load, and offline travel access; choose IMAP for multiple devices that need synchronization or server-side search.

cards.q: Why is POP3 a DLP consideration for network teams?
cards.a: Because mail data lands on endpoints rather than staying on servers, so network teams treat POP3 mostly as a traffic/permit need and a data-loss concern.

cards.q: How would you troubleshoot a can't-connect POP3 failure?
cards.a: Check whether TCP 110 is blocked by an ACL or firewall, verify credentials (-ERR auth), use 995 when TLS is required (connection reset), and confirm the server load/status on timeouts.

cards.q: Mail seems to vanish from a POP3 mailbox — why?
cards.a: POP3 downloads and deletes messages from the server by default; if retention is required, enable a keep-on-server option.
